questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix That Represents a Combination of Three Linear Transformations
questions.problem:
The matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 0 \\ 0 & b\end{aligned}]
$$

represents the linear transformation that acts on a vector in ${R}^{2}$ as follows (in the order given):

- It rotates the vector  $\pi $ radians counterclockwise about the origin, then

- stretches the result by a scale factor of $3$ parallel to the $x$-axis, and finally

- reflects the result about the $x$-axis.

What is the value of $a+b?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $P$ be the matrix that represents the rotation, $Q$ be the matrix that represents the stretching, and $R$ be the matrix that represents the reflection. These are given by the following elementary transformation matrices:

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,R=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Hence, the combined transformation can be represented by the matrix $RQP:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RQP & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,
$a+b=(-3)+1=-2.$

questions.problem:
Construct the matrix $T$ of the linear transformation $T$ that acts on a vector in ${R}^{2}$ as follows (in the order given):

- It rotates the vector by $\frac{\pi }{2}$ radians **clockwise** about the origin, then

- stretches the result by a scale factor of $5$ parallel to the $x$-axis, and finally

- shears the result with a shear factor of $3$ parallel to the $x$-axis.

|  |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $T=\,\,$ |  |  |  |  |
|  |  | {{field-3}} | $0$ |  |
questions.worked_solution:
Let $P$ be the matrix that represents the rotation, $Q$ be the matrix that represents the stretching, and $R$ be the matrix that represents the shearing. These are given by the following elementary transformation matrices:

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,R=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\,\,
$$

Hence, the combined transformation can be represented by the matrix $RQP:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =RQP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix That Represents a Combination of Two Linear Transformations
questions.problem:
Construct the matrix $T$ of the linear transformation $T$ that acts on a vector in ${R}^{2}$ as follows (in the order given):

- it shears the vector by a shear factor of $\frac{1}{3}$ parallel to the $x$-axis, and then

- scales the result by a scale factor of $3$ with center of enlargement at the origin.

|  |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $T=\,\,$ |  |  |  |  |
|  |  | $0$ | {{field-3}} |  |
questions.worked_solution:
Let $P$ be the matrix that represents the shear, and let $Q$ be the matrix that represents the scaling. These are given by the following elementary transformation matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\ Q & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the combined transformation can be represented by the matrix $QP:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =QP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Construct the matrix $T$ of the linear transformation $T$ that acts on a vector in ${R}^{2}$ as follows (in the order given):

- it shears the vector by a shear factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ parallel to the $y$-axis, and then

- scales the result by a scale factor of $4$ with center of enlargement at the origin.

|  |  | {{field-1}} | $0$ |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $T=\,\,$ |  |  |  |  |
|  |  | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} |  |
questions.worked_solution:
Let $P$ be the matrix that represents the shear, and let $Q$ be the matrix that represents the scaling. These are given by the following elementary transformation matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] \\ Q & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the combined transformation can be represented by the matrix $QP:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =QP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
